newsitem.title: UK: Mexican Bradies surge amid post-election calm.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Bradies surge amid post-election calm.

text.p: Mexican Brady bonds rallied on Monday as new found optimism in the country's electoral process sent prices soaring, emerging market traders said. "Because there was no bad news rather than that there was good news helped prices. We saw buyers out of Tokyo and general European account buyers of Mexico," said one Brady bond trader at a major U.S. investment bank in London.

Mexican UMS-26 MXUMS=RR extended earlier gains surging 1-3/4 to 118-1/2 bid. The country's par bonds MX625L19=RR also extended gains rising 3/4 to 80-1/4 bid as did its discount bonds MXFLL19=RR firming 5/8 to 94-1/2.

Unlike the impression after previous elections in Mexico, which have been fraught with allegations of voter fraud, market experts sighed relief on the fairness and largely peaceful outcome of the elections.

Preliminary results in Sunday's mid-term elections showed that the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) lost its 68-year control of the lower house of Congress, and was also trounced in the first ever mayoral race for Mexico City.
In the broader sector of the Brady market, traders said continued strong demand by traditional U.S. high-yield bond investors triggered spread narrowing across the board.

A strong U.S. Treasury market, a tame U.S. unemployment report on Thursday and the absence of a hike in U.S. interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve on Wednesday also added to the overall gains in the market, traders said.

"The scenario in Mexico is giving the market a little bit more confidence plus U.S. Treasuries had a great run on Thursday and this is giving the market an excuse to tighten even further," said another Brady bond trader at a European bank.

"There is pent-up demand and we have a tightening going on. If you take a look at the U.S. junk bond market, you will see that there is a real chase for yield at the moment and that is why our markets are tightening," said another trader.

Argentine Brady bonds also rose sharply following comments by the country's economy minister Roque Fernandez, who told Reuters in an interview in Buenos Aires that conditions were right for a debt buyback. Argentine pars AR4C23=RR were one percentage point higher at 72-5/8 bid and its discount bonds AR425C23=RR were 1-1/8 stronger at 88-5/8 bid. Fernandez also said the country's gross domestic product (GDP) for the second quarter would rise at least 5.0 percent from the second quarter in 1996. Among Eastern European credits, Bulgarian FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR were 1-1/8 higher at 60-3/4 bid and the country's IABs BGFLTH11=RR were 1-3/8 better at 76 bid.
